briefing.opening: Good morning. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 1, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Normalization of Extreme Weather and Domestic and International Heatwave Emergencies
sections.content: Globally, extreme weather phenomena such as heatwaves, wildfires, and floods are occurring simultaneously, signaling our entry into an era where 'extreme weather is becoming routine' [8]. In Europe, in particular, heatwaves have caused infrastructure crises, leading to efforts to introduce high-speed trains capable of withstanding 55 degrees Celsius [6], and Central Asia, including Kazakhstan, is also suffering from emergency extreme heat [9]. In Korea's Gyeongnam region, a record-breaking heatwave has continued since May 15, resulting in more heat-related illnesses than in Seoul [19]. On August 1, professional baseball games in Busan Sajik and Gyeongnam Changwon were canceled due to the heatwave [20], and sweltering heat with perceived temperatures around 35 degrees Celsius and tropical nights are expected in most parts of the country [24]. During such extreme heatwaves, the proportion of heat-related illness patients doubles even indoors [22], requiring special caution.

sections.title: ⚠️ Climate Crisis Frontline: Agricultural and Forest Disasters
sections.content: The climate crisis poses a direct threat to the agricultural and forestry sectors. The Jeju region is facing complex climate disasters, including severe drought and a shortage of agricultural water, which has disrupted carrot planting [3, 5], demonstrating that agriculture is on the frontline of the climate crisis [4]. Globally, we have entered an era of 'mega-fires,' with super-large wildfires equivalent to 29 atomic bombs occurring [2]. In France, large-scale wildfires displaced 200,000 people, and the midday temperature in the Le Porge area reached approximately 35 degrees Celsius [43]. As wildfires rage, ministers from various countries and UN leaders are urging climate action [35].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Carbon Neutrality Transition and New Dilemmas
sections.content: Domestically and internationally, efforts for carbon neutrality and renewable energy transition are actively continuing. Namseoul University successfully concluded a carbon neutrality sculpture exhibition at Lotte Mart Seongjeong branch [10, 11, 15], Ansan Green Environment Foundation held an operating committee for its Carbon Neutrality Support Center [12], and Gyeonggi Agricultural & Fisheries Institute is also promoting a carbon neutrality practice campaign [13], demonstrating ongoing efforts by local communities and institutions. NH Nonghyup Bank is expanding the role of the financial sector by issuing Korean-style green bonds that contribute to carbon neutrality and a green economy transition [14]. However, in Europe, a new dilemma has emerged where excessive solar power generation leads to negative electricity prices [16], and concerns are being raised that LNG, which has been used as a backup resource for renewable energy, could become a stranded asset in the long term [18]. Voices are also emerging from the Geoje City Council urging a shift in renewable energy policy [17].

sections.title: 🌍 Global Calls for Climate Action and Threats to Financial Stability
sections.content: The international community is emphasizing the importance of responding to the climate crisis, urging multifaceted discussions and actions. As wildfires raged, ministers from various countries and UN leaders raised their voices to call for climate action [35], and indigenous nations are demanding more power at the UN as climate change threatens their lands [39]. Meanwhile, Frank Elderson, a senior policymaker at the European Central Bank (ECB), warned that the climate emergency and nature collapse pose a rapidly increasing threat to the 'core financial stability' of the global economy [44], suggesting the need for a deeper understanding of how climate change makes droughts more frequent and severe [33, 36, 38]. Institutional responses are also being sought, with California beginning to solicit feedback on updated climate change reporting regulations [34]. The fact that Indian conglomerate Adani made massive profits from coal mines but paid no corporate tax [45] once again highlights issues of corporate responsibility related to climate justice.

sections.title: 📰 Importance of Climate Change Awareness and Adaptation
sections.content: Awareness of climate change and adaptation efforts are essential for the sustainability of our society. In Buenos Aires, the impact of climate change has also occurred, with the importance of caring for Korean residents being mentioned [1], and the effects of the climate crisis are also being observed on Germany's railways [7]. However, a Yale survey reports a decrease in Maine residents' concern about climate change [30], suggesting the need to raise public awareness. Meanwhile, in Vienna, Austria, cases of citizens adapting to climate change and enjoying summer, such as swimming in the 'Alte Donau' lake, are also being observed [25]. Experts recommend walks in the early morning or evening after the sun has set and temperatures have dropped during heatwaves [26], emphasizing the importance of individual adaptation efforts.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the various threats posed by climate change, alongside domestic and international efforts to overcome them, and new policy and social dilemmas. Continuous attention and action are required to respond to the era of climate crisis. This concludes today's climate briefing.
